items.item_text: resume
references
An advanced degree, professional fundraising certification, alumni relationship development, and/or higher-education fundraising campaign leadership experience are preferred.
A bachelor’s degree in any related field or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of Eight (8) years of progressively responsible experience as a development professional and manager in an innovative, forward-looking college environment is required.
An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience that provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the position may be considered.
Demonstrated record of strategic relationship development, major gifts fundraising success, and experience in the implementation and understanding of marketing techniques is required.

The Vice President is responsible for the development, implementation, and execution of strategic, annual, and operating plan goals and objectives related to the various Advancement functions; the determination of related performance metrics; and the measurement and evaluation of the Advancement’s performance against those goals.
Participate in strategic discussions and develop programs to strengthen the financial resources of the Institute.
The Vice President will develop short-term and long-range campaign strategies within Advancement and across other campus constituencies.

The Vice President directly supports the President and the Board of Trustees in fundraising activities and supports and coordinates the fundraising activities of the Institute’s academic and executive leadership.
Identify and secure partnerships with individuals, corporations, and foundations that can effectively support KGI’s philanthropic and community engagement goals.
Play a lead role in the education of all audiences so that they understand that philanthropy is a shared job and that philanthropy is essential for continued outstanding care.

Establish goals and objectives for campaign volunteer and staff structures, linking these goals with overall Advancement goals and fiscal year planning. Goals and objectives can be linked to tools, budgets, strategy, and metrics.
Partner with the President, Cabinet, and own team to engage deans, and faculty partners in campaign planning and goal attainment.
Maintain a dynamic portfolio of major gift prospects in all phases of qualifications.
Document and maintain clear and timely records and call reports to track contacts, donor giving, and notes, and assist in the maintenance of an accurate database.
Meet revenue goals for the institutional giving program as set by the President.
Support all giving efforts, including developing a department-wide yearly strategic plan.
Update policies, processes, and procedures for institutional giving and other policies as assigned.
Work with staff and key volunteers to develop, execute, and evaluate strategies to engage partners through outreach, education, invitations to special events, and personal contacts.
Develop and own the end-to-end alumni engagement strategy.
Establish and maintain alumni engagement activities (panels, awards ceremonies, networking events, reunions) that offer professional value to engage alumni around their professional needs.
Create coherent process where alumni engagement directly supports admissions, the student experience, academic excellence and corporate partnerships.

Engagement-to-Investment Pipeline: Actively identify and qualify high- potential alumni through their participation and volunteerism, converting general engagement into a tangible pipeline of philanthropic support, advocates and ambassadors.
Develop and own the end-to-end alumni engagement strategy.
Establish and maintain alumni engagement activities (panels, awards ceremonies, networking events, reunions) that offer professional value to engage alumni around their professional needs.
Supports the President in identifying and connecting with community partners, government leaders, professional partners, and prospective friends of the institution.
Serves on the President’s Cabinet.
Serve as Liaison for the Advancement and Marketing Committee of the Board of Trustees.
Other duties as assigned.
Highly motivated, goal-oriented, entrepreneurial self-starter who is a strategic and creative thinker who can work independently and, in a team, setting.
An open, transparent, and collaborative approach.
Demonstrated major gifts fundraising success and experience in the implementation and understanding of marketing techniques.
Outstanding interpersonal skills to identify and cultivate relationships to solicit and bring in significant contributions.
Strong analytical skills and ability to leverage fundraising data as a tool; experience with using and managing relationship management platform(s) (CRMs).
Clear and effective verbal and written communication with various faculty, staff, prospects, donors, vendors, and other stakeholders.

Clear understanding of the role of advancement within the broader context of the Institute and ability to articulate the case for support and to interact with institutional giving partners and prospects at the highest level.
Highly professional and ethical standards for handling confidential or sensitive information, including knowledge of nonprofit best practices.
Experience managing a team of diverse professionals with a focus on utilizing metrics, systems, and relationship building skills to maximize the cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donors.
Excellent project management skills and ability to balance competing priorities and complex situations.
Able and willing to work weekend and evening hours, as needed.
Flexibility and willingness to travel independently, 20% + local, and overnight/extended travel is required as needed to meet institutional goals.
